projectMilestones.title: Order operations and correctness contract
projectMilestones.description: Define the matching engine behavior before timing it. Order modification is supported only if included in the chosen contract.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: Add, cancel and execute operations have explicit expected behavior; supported modification semantics and corner cases are documented.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 2; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Implement the order operations
tasks.doneWhen: Add, cancel and execute orders according to a written contract; document whether modify is supported.

tasks.title: Test defined corner cases
tasks.doneWhen: Tests exercise the chosen order-book rules and reject invalid operations consistently.

projectMilestones.title: Deterministic replay and reference validation
projectMilestones.description: Keep a slower reference implementation to distinguish correctness from speed.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: The same event stream produces deterministic results and agrees with the slower reference.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 2; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Replay a deterministic event stream
tasks.doneWhen: Persist a controlled event stream or generator seed and verify reproducible engine outputs.

tasks.title: Compare with a reference engine
tasks.doneWhen: Validate the optimized candidate against the slower reference across the documented workloads.

projectMilestones.title: Controlled workloads and tail-latency baseline
projectMilestones.description: Measure a correct baseline under several workload distributions.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: Raw repeated measurements report throughput and p50/p95/p99 with workload, hardware and compiler configuration.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 2; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Pin the benchmark inputs
tasks.doneWhen: Record sizes, distributions, seeds and correctness checks for multiple controlled workloads.

tasks.title: Measure throughput and latency distribution
tasks.doneWhen: Use warmup and repeated runs; retain raw data and p50/p95/p99 rather than one best run.

tasks.title: Record the test environment
tasks.doneWhen: Capture hardware, compiler, optimization flags and how setup is excluded from measured work.

projectMilestones.title: Three measured optimization investigations
projectMilestones.description: Investigate layout, allocation, queue structure or other measured bottlenecks; keep regressions as evidence.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: At least three controlled changes have correctness checks, baseline/change measurements and explanations, including negative results.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 2; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Investigate at least three changes
tasks.doneWhen: For each hypothesis, change one controlled factor and rerun correctness and performance measurements.

tasks.title: Explain retained and rejected changes
tasks.doneWhen: Retain regressions and use profiler evidence to explain the resulting tradeoffs.

projectMilestones.title: Matching-engine portfolio exit review
projectMilestones.description: Review the whole project definition of done after the required work milestones, using saved evidence rather than reading or quiz progress.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: A correct replayable engine, reproducible workloads, throughput/tail latency, environment details and a profiler-backed optimization writeup are available.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 2; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Audit build, tests and replay instructions
tasks.doneWhen: A reader can build, run correctness tests and reproduce the controlled benchmarks from documented commands.

tasks.title: Audit the complete performance report
tasks.doneWhen: Review workload fairness, p50/p95/p99, throughput, hardware/compiler setup, profiler evidence and three investigations including regressions.

tasks.title: Prepare the project story
tasks.doneWhen: Write problem → baseline → hypothesis → optimization → actual results → limitations without unsupported speedup claims.

projectMilestones.title: Vector-add kernel and GPU timing
projectMilestones.description: Begin KernelForge with CUDA execution-model practice and a controlled timing method.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: Vector addition matches a CPU reference at boundary sizes and has reproducible GPU timing.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 3; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Implement and validate vector addition
tasks.doneWhen: Check CPU/GPU agreement, including inputs that do not evenly fill a block.

tasks.title: Separate kernel and transfer time
tasks.doneWhen: Document warmup, repetition and the boundaries of the GPU measurement.

projectMilestones.title: Parallel reduction
projectMilestones.description: Build a correct reduction before interpreting its bandwidth or occupancy.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: The reduction agrees with reference semantics/tolerances and is measured over controlled sizes.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 3; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Implement reduction with reference checks
tasks.doneWhen: Exercise several sizes and numerical edge cases using documented tolerances.

tasks.title: Record reduction measurements
tasks.doneWhen: Retain controlled repeated measurements and explain the measured data-access behavior.

projectMilestones.title: Parallel prefix scan
projectMilestones.description: Make inclusive/exclusive scan semantics explicit in the kernel suite.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: A parallel scan has documented semantics, reference validation and repeatable measurements.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 3; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Implement and test prefix scan
tasks.doneWhen: Document inclusive or exclusive behavior and validate edge and nonuniform input sizes against a reference.

tasks.title: Benchmark the validated scan
tasks.doneWhen: Record input configuration, timing boundaries and repeated results.

projectMilestones.title: Naive and shared-memory tiled GEMM
projectMilestones.description: Compare a naive matrix multiplication with a tiled implementation using controlled inputs.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: Both GEMM versions pass numerical checks; the effect of tiling is measured and explained.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 3; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Establish a correct naive GEMM
tasks.doneWhen: Validate matrix dimensions and reference tolerances before optimization.

tasks.title: Implement shared-memory tiling
tasks.doneWhen: Validate the tiled kernel and compare it with the naive baseline under the same inputs.

projectMilestones.title: Convolution or related compute-heavy kernel
projectMilestones.description: Choose one additional compute-heavy kernel; this is not a requirement to build several unrelated kernels.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: One convolution or related kernel has reference tests and measured behavior.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 3; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Implement the selected kernel
tasks.doneWhen: Document the operation and validate its output against a meaningful reference.

tasks.title: Measure a controlled kernel experiment
tasks.doneWhen: Use fixed inputs and reproducible timing to explain a relevant bottleneck or optimization.

projectMilestones.title: Meaningful CPU and NVIDIA library comparisons
projectMilestones.description: Use relevant optimized baselines rather than an intentionally weak CPU implementation.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: Comparisons use a relevant optimized CPU baseline and NVIDIA libraries where sensible, including cuBLAS for GEMM.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 3; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Establish a fair CPU comparison
tasks.doneWhen: Document the CPU implementation, hardware, precision and workload; avoid a deliberately unoptimized baseline.

tasks.title: Compare with relevant NVIDIA libraries
tasks.doneWhen: Include cuBLAS for GEMM and explain where library comparisons are or are not applicable.

projectMilestones.title: Nsight bottleneck experiments
projectMilestones.description: Use profiler evidence to interpret memory traffic, bandwidth and occupancy where meaningful.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: Nsight evidence supports the reported bottlenecks and measured optimizations.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 3; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Profile meaningful kernel workloads
tasks.doneWhen: Capture memory bandwidth, bottlenecks and occupancy where relevant on a compatible NVIDIA system.

tasks.title: Explain optimization outcomes
tasks.doneWhen: Connect profiler observations to raw benchmark data, including unsuccessful changes and limitations.

projectMilestones.title: KernelForge portfolio exit review
projectMilestones.description: Review the complete correct, reproducible kernel suite and technical report.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: Vector addition, reduction, scan, naive/tiled GEMM and a compute-heavy kernel have tests, fair baselines, measured optimizations and a technical report.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 3; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Audit the complete kernel suite
tasks.doneWhen: Confirm all listed kernels and reproducible correctness/benchmark commands are included.

tasks.title: Audit baseline and profiler evidence
tasks.doneWhen: Review CPU/library fairness, precision, transfer/kernel boundaries, Nsight data and measurement variation.

tasks.title: Publish an evidence-based technical report
tasks.doneWhen: Explain problem, baseline, hypothesis, changes, actual results and limitations with setup instructions and retained raw data.

projectMilestones.title: Supported model and reference baseline
projectMilestones.description: Choose a small supported model and a compatible NVIDIA environment before serving experiments.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: The exact model, held-out accuracy test and latency baseline are recorded with environment/precision details.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 4; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Confirm model and tool compatibility
tasks.doneWhen: Record the selected small model and compatible GPU, driver, CUDA and TensorRT environment.

tasks.title: Measure reference accuracy and latency
tasks.doneWhen: Fix the test set/model version and retain reference metrics plus a controlled latency baseline.

projectMilestones.title: C++ inference runtime and end-to-end correctness
projectMilestones.description: Build the runtime with TensorRT where compatible with the chosen environment.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: A working C++ runtime runs the selected model end to end and passes reference correctness checks.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 4; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Build the C++ runtime
tasks.doneWhen: Load and run the supported model in the documented compatible NVIDIA environment.

tasks.title: Validate the serving path
tasks.doneWhen: Check preprocessing/inference outputs and numerical tolerances against the reference.

projectMilestones.title: Custom CUDA preprocessing
projectMilestones.description: Integrate preprocessing without silently changing model input semantics.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: CUDA preprocessing matches the reference and is included in separate and end-to-end timing boundaries.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 4; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Implement and validate preprocessing
tasks.doneWhen: Compare CUDA-produced model inputs with the reference implementation on controlled cases.

tasks.title: Measure preprocessing in the pipeline
tasks.doneWhen: Record its compute/transfer contribution without hiding it from end-to-end latency.

projectMilestones.title: Batching, streams and overlap experiments
projectMilestones.description: Study request queueing, batching policy, stream behavior and asynchronous transfers under load.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: Controlled experiments explain batching/stream/overlap tradeoffs without sacrificing correctness.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 4; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Explore batching and request load
tasks.doneWhen: Compare documented batching policies at multiple load levels with correctness and latency checks.

tasks.title: Explore streams and transfer overlap
tasks.doneWhen: Use CUDA streams/events and profiler evidence to measure asynchronous execution and overlap.

projectMilestones.title: Throughput versus latency curves
projectMilestones.description: Report throughput and tail latency together, separating queueing, transfers and compute.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: Multiple controlled load levels produce reproducible throughput/latency curves and p95/p99 with fair baselines.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 4; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Generate controlled load curves
tasks.doneWhen: Retain repeated measurements across load levels, reporting throughput and p95/p99 rather than only peak throughput.

tasks.title: Audit timing and baseline fairness
tasks.doneWhen: Separate setup, preprocessing, transfers, inference and end-to-end response time; pin model/precision/test inputs.

projectMilestones.title: Supported precision/accuracy experiment
projectMilestones.description: Where supported, evaluate FP32/FP16/INT8 changes with the exact accuracy test set. Unsupported paths are limitations, not measured results.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: A supported precision change has measured quality/performance tradeoffs on the fixed test set, with numerical conventions documented.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 4; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Evaluate a supported precision change
tasks.doneWhen: Use the exact held-out accuracy set and document numerical error/quality changes.

tasks.title: Measure the supported tradeoff
tasks.doneWhen: Compare controlled timing and throughput at the selected precisions without claiming unsupported modes.

projectMilestones.title: Inference-runtime portfolio exit review
projectMilestones.description: Audit the working runtime, profiler evidence and fair comparisons; optional precision studies must be labeled by actual support.
projectMilestones.doneWhen: The runtime works end to end with tests, profiler data, loaded-system curves, a documented baseline and accuracy/precision limitations.
projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phase 4; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Audit runtime setup and correctness
tasks.doneWhen: A reader can configure the compatible environment and run end-to-end correctness tests.

tasks.title: Audit complete inference measurements
tasks.doneWhen: Review batching/streams/overlap, throughput/latency curves, accuracy, precision used and limitations with raw data.

tasks.title: Prepare the runtime demonstration and story
tasks.doneWhen: Record a working demo and write actual baseline/hypothesis/results/limitations without unsupported improvement claims.

projectMilestones.title: Verified RTL building blocks
projectMilestones.description: The early parallel FPGA exercises are milestones of this capstone, not extra portfolio projects.

tasks.title: Verify counters, FSM and 8-bit ALU

tasks.title: Verify signed fixed-point MAC behavior
tasks.doneWhen: Document overflow/saturation, reset/clock semantics and pipeline behavior against a numerical model.

projectMilestones.title: Pipelined dot product and synthesis reports
projectMilestones.description: Connect pipelining/HLS scheduling choices to actual resources and timing.

projectMilestones.sourceSection: ROADMAP.md §3 Phases 5–6 and parallel FPGA track; §9 measurement rules; §10 master checklist

tasks.title: Synthesize a validated dot product
tasks.doneWhen: Check known vectors and produce a synthesis report using a compatible toolchain.

tasks.title: Interpret resource and timing tradeoffs
tasks.doneWhen: Record achieved timing, II and utilization; explain clock constraints, critical-path/slack, reset/clock-domain risks and measured PIPELINE/UNROLL/partitioning or pipeline choices.

projectMilestones.title: Fixed-point FIR or preprocessing block
projectMilestones.description: Verify a reusable arithmetic block within the same capstone; final integration depends on data-path value.

tasks.title: Implement the fixed-point block
tasks.doneWhen: Document its representation and verify outputs against a C++ reference.

tasks.title: Record known-vector and corner-case tests
tasks.doneWhen: Retain test inputs/outputs and describe pipeline or resource tradeoffs; explain whether integration helps.

tasks.title: Confirm the supported board build flow

tasks.title: Compare hardware outputs with the reference

roadmapMeta.title: Silicon Quest
roadmapMeta.northStar: Become a hardware-aware performance engineer who designs, measures and optimizes low-level systems across CPUs, NVIDIA GPUs and FPGAs.
roadmapMeta.moduleNotice: Provisional topic modules derived from the roadmap, not verified textbook chapters. Selective study supports projects; completing every book is not required.
roadmapMeta.seedProgress: No milestone is marked complete without implementation evidence.

budget.note: Historical planning assumptions; excludes tax, commercial books and board/workstation costs. Recheck official prices before purchasing.

hardwareNotes: Apple Silicon supports local C++/Python experiments; native CUDA requires a compatible NVIDIA environment.
Verify supported x86-64 Linux/Windows Vivado/Vitis/PYNQ versions and board files.
PYNQ-Z2 is for compact networks; resize based on actual synthesis.
Verify hls4ml support; modern FINN does not officially target PYNQ-Z2 in this roadmap.
firstMonth: Week 1: CMake/CTest, compiler/sanitizers, microbenchmark; binary arithmetic and counter testbench.
Week 2: AoS/SoA and sequential/random experiments; FSM and 8-bit ALU simulation.
Week 3: allocation, branch prediction and data movement; fixed-point MAC simulation.
Week 4: technical note with graphs/tests/limitations; engine correctness contract and dated CUDA/FPGA access plan.

modules.title: Caches & locality
modules.summary: Connect working-set size and access pattern to measured CPU behavior.
modules.exercise: Benchmark sequential and random traversal over several array sizes.
modules.doneWhen: Correctness checks, raw repeated timings, hardware details and an explanation of the observed trend.

modules.title: AoS vs SoA
modules.summary: Explore how contiguous storage and layout change data movement.
modules.exercise: Implement equivalent AoS and SoA computations and benchmark them.
modules.doneWhen: Matching outputs and at least two controlled input sizes with raw timings.

modules.title: RAII & move semantics
modules.summary: Reason about C++20 object lifetime and ownership before measuring performance.
modules.exercise: Write a small resource-owning type and inspect copy/move behavior.
modules.doneWhen: Lifetime tests pass and ownership behavior is explained without claiming unmeasured speedups.

modules.title: Allocation strategies
modules.summary: Compare allocation choices using the same workload.
modules.exercise: Compare baseline allocation with a pool or reserved contiguous storage.
modules.doneWhen: Correct outputs, controlled inputs and repeated baseline/change measurements.

modules.title: Reliable microbenchmarks
modules.summary: Establish reproducible measurements before optimization.
modules.exercise: Build a C++ benchmark harness with a correctness test and raw result output.
modules.doneWhen: CMake/CTest workflow, warmup, repeat counts and reproducible benchmark invocation are documented.

modules.title: Processes & virtual memory
modules.summary: Build an OS-level explanation of memory behavior.
objectives: Distinguish process address spaces and physical memory
modules.exercise: Record a small process-memory experiment and relate observations to its access pattern.
modules.doneWhen: Test setup and observed results are recorded with clear limitations.

modules.title: Atomics & contention
modules.summary: Understand queues, ordering and shared cache lines.
modules.exercise: Implement a tested SPSC queue or contention experiment for the engine pipeline.
modules.doneWhen: Deterministic correctness evidence and a controlled contention benchmark are available.

modules.title: Matching-engine experiments
modules.summary: Optimize against a correct replayable engine baseline.
modules.exercise: Investigate at least three layout, allocation or queue changes.
modules.doneWhen: Reference validation, workload distributions, throughput/tail latency and a report include regressions.

modules.title: CUDA execution model
modules.summary: Map work to threads, warps and blocks.
modules.exercise: Implement vector addition with CPU reference validation.
modules.doneWhen: Correct output for boundary sizes and a reproducible GPU timing method.

modules.title: Coalescing & bandwidth
modules.summary: Measure data-access behavior and asynchronous transfer boundaries.
modules.exercise: Compare controlled GPU access patterns and capture Nsight evidence.
modules.doneWhen: Correctness, memory-traffic interpretation and repeatable measured results.

modules.title: Reduction & prefix scan
modules.summary: Practice parallel aggregation with explicit correctness checks.
modules.exercise: Implement reduction and parallel prefix scan for several input sizes.
modules.doneWhen: Reference checks including edge cases and performance measurements for both kernels.

modules.title: Tiled GEMM & convolution
modules.summary: Explore shared-memory tiling and relevant optimized baselines.
modules.exercise: Implement naive/tiled GEMM and one convolution or related compute-heavy kernel.
modules.doneWhen: Correct results, relevant CPU/library comparisons and profiler-backed discussion.

modules.title: Quantitative bottlenecks
modules.summary: Use measured workload behavior to study hardware limits.
modules.exercise: Explain a KernelForge bottleneck using measurements and architecture concepts.
modules.doneWhen: Profiler evidence supports the bottleneck claim and caveats are documented.

modules.title: Serving, streams & batching
modules.summary: Measure end-to-end inference under realistic load.
modules.exercise: Build the C++/TensorRT runtime with custom CUDA preprocessing where supported.
modules.doneWhen: Correct runtime plus throughput/latency curves across multiple load levels.

modules.title: Logic, counters & FSMs
modules.summary: Begin the FPGA track with simulation.
modules.exercise: Simulate a counter, FSM and 8-bit ALU.
modules.doneWhen: Corner-case checks pass; no physical bitstream is required at this stage.

modules.title: Fixed-point & pipelined MAC
modules.summary: Make numerical and pipeline behavior explicit.
modules.exercise: Model and simulate a fixed-point MAC with pipeline registers.
modules.doneWhen: Self-checking known vectors pass and reset/clock semantics are explained.

modules.title: Synthesis & timing reports
modules.summary: Connect RTL structure to hardware resource and timing constraints.
modules.exercise: Synthesize the pipelined MAC if compatible tools are available.
modules.doneWhen: Simulation evidence plus a synthesis report, or an explicit tooling blocker without invented results.

modules.title: HLS pipelining & partitioning
modules.summary: Compare hardware scheduling choices within the one capstone.
modules.exercise: Synthesize a pipelined dot product and compare one HLS scheduling change.
modules.doneWhen: Numerical checks and measured LUT/FF/DSP/BRAM, timing and II are recorded.

modules.title: Fixed-point FIR block
modules.summary: Build a small reusable arithmetic block for the capstone.
modules.exercise: Implement a fixed-point FIR or preprocessing block against a C++ reference.
modules.doneWhen: Known vectors pass and the role of the block in the capstone is documented.

modules.title: Zynq PS, PL & overlays
modules.summary: Understand the host/accelerator split and supported tool flow.
objectives: Distinguish processing system and programmable logic
modules.exercise: Survey compatible PYNQ-Z2 build/runtime versions and identify the development machine.
modules.doneWhen: A dated compatibility decision and tool-access plan exist.

modules.title: AXI, DMA & buffers
modules.summary: Move verified data between ARM and programmable logic.
modules.exercise: Load a supported overlay and round-trip known vectors through the data path.
modules.doneWhen: Physical PYNQ-Z2 output matches reference; core and transfer timing are separated.

modules.title: Quantization & accuracy
modules.summary: Measure precision changes against a held-out reference.
objectives: Record scales/zero points or fixed-point format
modules.exercise: Train FP32 and quantize the compact gesture classifier to INT8.
modules.doneWhen: Train/validation/test separation, FP32/INT8 metrics and confusion matrix are recorded.

modules.title: Fit-to-device inference
modules.summary: Deploy a compact network based on real synthesis constraints.
modules.exercise: Use a confirmed hls4ml flow or a small handwritten HLS datapath and deploy to PYNQ-Z2.
modules.doneWhen: Physical-board demo, design/driver source, accuracy, resource/timing and fair benchmark reports.

modules.title: Revisit measured bottlenecks
modules.summary: Choose deeper study using evidence from completed projects.
objectives: Connect pipelines and precision to results
modules.exercise: Write one focused architecture note linked to a real project bottleneck.
modules.doneWhen: The note cites project evidence, limitations and a testable next hypothesis.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which evidence best supports a performance improvement claim?
choices: One fastest run after editing the code
Correctness checks, a controlled baseline, repeated measurements and recorded configuration
A profiler screenshot without the input or hardware details
A larger input for only the optimized version
quizQuestions.explanation: Correctness, controlled inputs, repeated timing and a recorded environment make the comparison interpretable and reproducible. A single best run hides variance.

quizQuestions.prompt: Why might sequential traversal outperform random traversal of the same array?
choices: Sequential order guarantees every access hits L1
Random traversal always uses more arithmetic
Sequential access can improve locality and let prefetching anticipate future accesses
The compiler must remove all sequential loads
quizQuestions.explanation: Sequential access often uses nearby elements in each fetched cache line and gives hardware prefetchers a predictable pattern. The actual result still depends on working-set size and hardware.

quizQuestions.prompt: What is the central idea of RAII?
choices: Tie resource ownership to object lifetime so destruction releases the resource
Move every object to avoid allocation
Use global variables for every resource
Manually release resources after every expression
quizQuestions.explanation: RAII connects resource acquisition and release to object construction and destruction. It helps maintain correct cleanup across normal control flow and exceptions.

quizQuestions.prompt: Why report p95/p99 as well as throughput?
choices: Percentiles eliminate all measurement noise
Throughput alone proves every request is fast
Tail percentiles measure source-code complexity
Aggregate throughput can hide slow requests in the latency distribution
quizQuestions.explanation: Throughput measures work completed per time interval. Tail-latency percentiles describe the slower requests, which can matter even when aggregate throughput looks good.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which adjacent-thread access pattern is generally favorable for coalescing?
choices: Each thread accesses an unrelated allocation
Adjacent threads access adjacent suitably aligned elements
Every thread serially reads the full input
Every warp uses a different numerical precision
quizQuestions.explanation: Nearby addresses requested by neighboring threads can be served efficiently by memory transactions. Alignment and the precise access pattern matter; measure the real kernel.

quizQuestions.prompt: A pipeline has latency 5 cycles and initiation interval 1. What does that imply?
choices: Every result takes only 1 cycle from input
Only one input may enter every 5 cycles
It can accept a new input each cycle, with each result emerging 5 cycles later
Its clock frequency is exactly 5 GHz
quizQuestions.explanation: Latency is the input-to-output delay; initiation interval is the spacing between accepted inputs. They are different quantities, and neither alone determines clock frequency.

quizQuestions.prompt: What is needed for a fair FPGA latency report?
choices: Report core compute and data-transfer/end-to-end timing separately
Report only the HLS estimated cycle count as host latency
Exclude all numerical checks
Assume DMA has zero overhead
quizQuestions.explanation: The arithmetic pipeline and the ARM/host/DMA path have different timing boundaries. Reporting both shows whether data movement dominates the actual application.

quizQuestions.prompt: After quantizing a model to INT8, what should be checked?
choices: Only that the output tensor exists
Only that the model file is smaller
Training accuracy on the same data used to tune quantization
Held-out accuracy, numerical conventions, resource use and measured performance
quizQuestions.explanation: Lower precision changes numerical behavior as well as storage and compute costs. Evaluate on a held-out set, document scales/zero points or fixed-point conventions, and measure the actual target.

measurementRules: Establish correctness against a reference before optimizing.
Pin input sizes, seeds, model versions, precision, compiler flags and hardware.
Separate setup, transfer, compute and end-to-end response time.
Warm up appropriately; repeat measurements and report distribution/variance.
Use fair optimized CPU and relevant GPU-library baselines.
Separate FPGA pipeline latency from ARM/host/DMA overhead.
Report numerical accuracy and resource/energy methodology when changing precision.
Retain failed or regressing experiments with explanations.
Store scripts and raw benchmark data with charts.
